verdict.rationale: Sill's docs state there is no account and no server, and that screen and input travel only between your own devices. Devices pair once by scanning a code or over USB, and only paired devices can connect, with every connection encrypted. Sessions move onto your home network by themselves, and Direct Wireless Connection works even without shared Wi-Fi. Missing for 10: an explicit description of how devices automatically discover the host on the local network (the mechanism is only implied), and independent or hands-on corroboration beyond the vendor's own docs.

support.subject: As a power user, my devices find the host on the local network and connect without an account or a vendor server in between

citations.quote: There is no account and no server: your screen and what you type travel only between your own devices
when you get home, the session moves to your network by itself
it shows a code for your iPhone or iPad to scan, and over a USB cable the two pair by themselves.
Direct Wireless Connection lets an iPhone or iPad near your Mac connect without a shared Wi-Fi network, the way AirDrop does.
After that, only the devices you paired can connect, and every connection is encrypted.
